newsitem.title: USA: Perjury trial postponed for former Arkansas banker.
newsitem.headline: Perjury trial postponed for former Arkansas banker.

text.p: The perjury trial of former Arkansas investment banker Preston Bynum has been postponed while he recovers from heart surgery, defense attorney Jack Lassiter said Tuesday.
Bynum had been scheduled to stand trial Monday before U.S. District Judge Lacey Coller. Instead, he underwent heart bypass surgery Monday in Little Rock, Ark.
"He got through his surgery well, I'm happy to say," Lassiter said.
The trial was reset for Aug. 4, a U.S. Attorney's spokeswoman said.

Bynum previously worked for Arkansas underwriter Stephens Inc. He was charged in 1995 with lying to the Pensacola, Fla., grand jury that indicted him on charges that he bribed an Escambia County, Fla., Utility Authority official to win municipal bond business.
The perjury indictment remain sealed until February, 1997.
Bynum pleaded guilty in March 1995 to a bribery count and served two years in a federal prison.
He was also barred from the securities industry for life and ordered to pay a $250,000 fine to settle a civil fraud charge that the Securities and Exchange Commission levied in the case.
If convicted of perjury, Bynum could face up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
